identification.summary: Earth Lamia is Trend Micro's name for a China-nexus intrusion set that Trend Research says has been active since at least 2023 and that mainly exploits web application vulnerabilities [S1][S3]. Google Threat Intelligence Group tracks Earth Lamia as UNC5454 [S4]. Microsoft has no mapping in this record; no Microsoft name was found.
identification.firstObserved: At least 2023 (Trend Micro) [S1][S3]. The PULSEPACK backdoor was first seen in attacks in August 2024 [S3].
identification.notes: Trend Micro names Earth Lamia; GTIG uses UNC5454 [S4]. Trend Micro reportedly links the cluster to REF0657 (Elastic), STAC6451 (Sophos) and CL-STA-0048 (Unit 42), per a search summary of the Trend report; the original report page could not be opened to confirm [S1]. Keep these as vendor-cluster overlaps, not merged facts. AWS names Earth Lamia and, separately, Jackpot Panda; GTIG says no public indicators exist to assess a relationship between them [S4][S5].

attribution.confidence: Trend Micro assesses the activity as a China-nexus intrusion set [S1]. GTIG and AWS describe related React2Shell exploitation as China-nexus; GTIG states the Earth Lamia/Jackpot Panda link comes from AWS reporting, not its own assessment [S4][S5]. AWS notes shared anonymization infrastructure among Chinese groups makes definitive attribution challenging [S5]. No government attribution found.
attribution.basis: Trend Micro research evidence (details not verified here) [S1]; AWS honeypot observations of exploitation attempts from infrastructure historically linked to named groups [S5].

targeting.notes: Trend Micro says targeting has shifted over time from financial services, to logistics and online retail, and most recently to IT firms, universities and government organizations [S1][S3]. An aggregator (strobes.co) also lists Latin America and the Middle East; that is not confirmed in Trend Micro coverage seen here.

capabilities.summary: Initial access is mainly through exploitation of web application flaws, frequently scanning for SQL injection (Trend Micro suspects sqlmap) and exploiting known vulnerabilities in public-facing servers [S1][S3]. Trend Micro lists CVE-2024-27198 (JetBrains TeamCity), CVE-2024-51378 (CyberPanel) and CVE-2025-31324 (SAP NetWeaver Visual Composer) among exploited flaws [S1]. Custom tooling includes the modular .NET backdoor PULSEPACK (TCP C2 in 2024) and the privilege-escalation tool BypassBoss [S1][S3]. The group uses DLL sideloading to run Cobalt Strike and Brute Ratel shellcode [S1][S3]. AWS reported Earth Lamia exploiting React2Shell (CVE-2025-55182) within hours of its 3 December 2025 disclosure [S5][S4].

campaigns.name: Financial services targeting
campaigns.summary: Trend Micro says the cluster initially focused on financial services organizations; a secondary write-up places this in 2023 to early 2024 [S1][S3].

campaigns.name: PULSEPACK first observed
campaigns.summary: Trend Micro first saw the previously unseen PULSEPACK backdoor in attacks in August 2024, with TCP-based C2 [S3].

campaigns.name: Logistics and online retail focus
campaigns.summary: Targeting shifted to logistics and online retail, per Trend Micro [S1][S3].

campaigns.name: Trend Micro public reporting
campaigns.summary: Trend Micro published its Earth Lamia report describing recent focus on IT companies, universities and government in Brazil, India and Southeast Asia [S1][S3].

campaigns.name: React2Shell (CVE-2025-55182) exploitation
campaigns.summary: AWS reported China-nexus groups including Earth Lamia and Jackpot Panda began exploiting the flaw within hours of the 3 December 2025 disclosure; GTIG relayed the AWS finding and gave no UNC5454-specific tooling [S4][S5].

diamond.adversary: China-nexus intrusion set tracked as Earth Lamia (Trend Micro) and UNC5454 (GTIG); operator identity and sponsor not established in sources gathered [S1][S4].
diamond.capability: Web application exploitation, SQL injection, PULSEPACK, BypassBoss, DLL sideloading, Cobalt Strike and Brute Ratel [S1][S3].
diamond.victim: Financial, logistics, retail, IT, education and government organizations in Brazil, India and Southeast Asia [S1][S3].
diamond.technology: Internet-facing web applications and servers with unpatched or SQL-injectable flaws (TeamCity, CyberPanel, SAP NetWeaver, React Server Components) [S1][S5].

gaps: Trend Micro's primary report, AWS's primary blog and the Google Cloud and trade-press pages could not be fully opened (fetch failures); several details rest on search-result summaries and should be verified against the originals.
Sponsor, tasking and objectives are not stated in sources gathered.
Attribution rests on vendor assessments; AWS notes definitive attribution is challenging due to shared infrastructure [S5].

Overlaps with REF0657 (Elastic), STAC6451 (Sophos, which deployed Mimic ransomware) and CL-STA-0048 (Unit 42) not independently confirmed; Earth Lamia itself has not been observed using ransomware per Trend Micro summary [S1].
Relationship between Earth Lamia and Jackpot Panda is unknown; GTIG says no public indicators [S4].
No Microsoft actor name found; MITRE group ID not assigned in this record.
Infrastructure details and indicators not gathered.
Forescout's Chaya_004 (SAP NetWeaver CVE-2025-31324 exploitation) was not linked to Earth Lamia in any source found; do not merge.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Internet-facing web applications, developer/CI servers (TeamCity), hosting control panels, ERP middleware (SAP NetWeaver) and React/Next.js servers are key terrain, especially for IT, university and government organizations in Brazil, India and Southeast Asia [S1][S5]. STEP 2: Exploitation within hours of disclosure (React2Shell) narrows the patch window to near zero [S5]. STEP 3: Template is web-app exploit or SQL injection, then PULSEPACK or Cobalt Strike/Brute Ratel via DLL sideloading, then privilege escalation with BypassBoss [S1][S3]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued opportunistic exploitation of newly disclosed web flaws against regional IT, education and government targets. MDCOA is use of compromised IT service providers or partner government networks as a path to coalition or DoD-adjacent partners in the region. Candidate indicators: SQL injection scanning against web apps, DLL sideloading by legitimate signed binaries, and unexpected Cobalt Strike/Brute Ratel beacons [S1][S3].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track exploited-vulnerability advisories for web frameworks and enterprise middleware and push mitigation status to partner networks in Southeast Asia and Latin America. (2) Authorities: partner-network hunting depends on host-nation consent and DCO authorities; coordinate before action outside DODIN. (3) Mission assurance: prioritize patching and WAF coverage of internet-facing apps supporting mission systems and contractors. (4) Coordination: share indicators with DC3 and allied CERTs; note attribution is vendor-level and clusters overlap, so prioritize containment over naming [S4].
